prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1016; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep it brief. Can you tell me where the collision happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, near a shopping center entrance.
Q: What were you doing right before it happened?
A: I was driving home from work. Traffic was light, maybe thirty miles an hour.
Q: Can you describe the other vehicle and how the impact occurred?
A: It was coming toward me in my lane. The driver had drifted over the center line. We both braked, but there wasn't much room, and the fronts of the cars met. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was definitely a head-on.
Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, they didn't. I was jolted forward and then slammed back into the seat.
Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?
A: My neck felt stiff right away, and by the next morning I had pain running into my shoulders. I also had a headache.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same evening, and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week since then.
Q: Have you had any prior neck or back complaints?
A: Not that required treatment. I had some stiffness now and then after long desk days, but nothing like this.
Q: Is there anything you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble turning my head to check mirrors, and it's affecting my ability to work comfortably.
Q: Thank you. That concludes our statement.
A: Alright, thanks.
